source.quote: Count the stars from Krittika in groups of nine. The planets presiding over the dasas belonging to the nine nakshatras composing each group are respectively the Sun, the Moon, Mars, Rahu, Jupiter, Saturn, Mercury, Ketu and Venus and the span of their dasa periods are respectively 6, 10, 7, 18, 16, 19, 17, 7 and 20 year.

cards.note: The full Vimshottari scheme in one sentence: which nine grahas preside, in which order, for how many years each (6+10+7+18+16+19+17+7+20 = 120, the whole cycle), and that the 27 nakshatras are grouped in threes-of-nine starting from Krittika (the second nakshatra by this book's own zero-based order -- Ashwini, Bharani, Krittika -- read from `Engine.chart.NAKSHATRAS`, which is coordinate bookkeeping, not a further claim this card makes). Consulted by `Doctrine.vimshottari_periods` (Engine/doctrine.py), read by the `_dasa` extractor (Engine/facts.py) and `Engine/dasa.py`'s sequence arithmetic rather than either being a Python literal.

source.quote: Note the exact position of the Sun in the Zodiac at the time of birth when the Sun in his next round arrives at the same position, it is considered as a solar year, which is also the year taken for Udu adasa system (Vimsottari or naksharta dasa system). By subdividing the same, days are calculated.

source.quote: Now-a-days the easiest method of the remainder of the dasa accordingly is based on the longitude of the Moon 3-13°-12' (Cancer 13°-12'). Cancer is composed of one quater or 3°-20' of Punarvasu, four quarters of Ashlesha. As the longitude of 13°-12' in Cancer, it has passed the fourth quarter of Punarvasu in this […] sign and is in Pushyami nakshatra. To find out how much it has moved in Pushyami we will deduct 3°-20' of Punarvasu from the Moon's 13°-12'. Thus the balance will come to 9°-52'. The extent of the whole of Pushyami is 13°-20'. The lord of this nakshatra is Saturn whose total dasa period is 19 years. Therefore 13°- 20' being equal to 19 years, 9°-52' will be equal to 14 years 0 months of 22 days. This indicates that the 14 years and 22 days are observed over at birth and that would remain at credit at birth will be 19 years minus 14 years 22 days, that is, 4 years 11 months and 8 days.

cards.note: The translator's Notes, not the root verse: v.3's printed root text states Mantreswara's own division-by-60 shortcut (`PD.19.BalanceMethod.Mantreswara`, linked by `contradicts`), and the Notes go on to reject it explicitly ('This in our view is not correct as the total number of ghatikas are not always 60') before giving this degree-based restatement of what the Notes call 'the generally recognised method' -- the same proportion, in a unit the engine already has (`BodyState.lon`) rather than ghatikas. Quoted in two spans because the printed passage crosses a page break (p.175/176) mid-sentence, the same `dep.multi-span-quote` pattern used elsewhere in this store. This is a *worked example*, not itself a general table; `Engine/dasa.py::balance_at_birth_years` restates its proportion algebraically (verified against these exact numbers in `Engine/tests/test_dasa.py`) rather than reading a per-case lookup, since there is nothing table-shaped to look up -- one universal proportion, not a value that varies by mobility, varga or authority the way `PD.03.Navamsa.Start`'s offsets do. Because neither this card nor `PD.19.BalanceMethod.Mantreswara` ever fires as a claim (both are the engine's own justification for a computation, not a rule about a nativity), the `contradicts` link between them is documentary in the rule store and in `Reports/`, and does not surface in a per-chart consultation -- `Engine.adjudicate` only reports a declared link when at least one side has activated a claim (see its own docstring), and a computation-method dispute has no claim for either side to attach to.

source.quote: Now is described the method of finding the remainder of the dasa of planet at the time of birth. Find out the nakshatra in which the Moon is posited at birth and for how many ghatikas it will remain after birth in that nakshatra. Multiply those ghatikas by the total period of the dasa and divide it by 60. The quotient will represent the period in years still to elapse. Any remainder remaining may be converted into months by multiplying by 30 and dividing by 60 and so on.

cards.note: The root verse's own printed method, identified by its own Notes (same verse) as 'the method of calculation according to Shri Mantreshwar' -- always dividing by 60 regardless of the nakshatra's true span -- and as the reading the translator rejects ('not correct as the total number of ghatikas are not always 60'). Preserved rather than deleted: this is the source's own stated method, on record, and `PD.19.BalanceMethod` carries the reading the engine actually computes with. This card's own `method` is never queried by a `Doctrine` accessor and never becomes a claim -- it drives no computation -- so its `relation` is deliberately distinct from `dasa_balance_method` (no accessor could accidentally read the disputed value instead of the endorsed one). Its `measured_from` field is a different matter: this root sentence -- 'find out the nakshatra in which the Moon is posited at birth' -- is the instruction *both* balance methods share (only the division step differs), so it is the one place in the chapter that names which body the whole of dep.dasa keys on. Read by a new `Doctrine.dasa_measured_from` accessor and consulted by the `_dasa` extractor (Engine/facts.py), so the engine never writes 'Moon' as a literal -- the same discipline `combustion_source` already applies to the Sun.

source.quote: During the dasa of the Mars there will be, on the part of the native, efforts to earn money through lands, litigation and the king. He will acquire agricultural lands and cattle. There will be enmity with his son and brothers and he will be attached to women of ill fame. He will suffer from impurity of blood, diseases arising from heat and loss through fire. There will also be loss of wealth.
